faqs.question: What makes a good real estate website?
faqs.answer: A good real estate website loads fast on a phone, shows the project's location, configuration, price band, possession date and RERA number early, has real photos and floor plans with carpet area, and makes it one tap to start a WhatsApp chat or book a site visit. Clear facts beat fancy design.

faqs.question: What features should a real estate website have?
faqs.answer: Every real estate site needs RERA numbers for registered projects, a price band, floor plans with carpet area, a map with travel times, WhatsApp and call buttons, a short form, dated construction updates, FAQs and conversion tracking. Search filters, virtual tours, EMI details and an NRI section depend on your buyers.

faqs.question: What types of real estate websites are there?
faqs.answer: There are four main types: a developer brand site, a project microsite or landing page for each project, a broker or channel partner site with locality pages and listings, and portal listings on sites such as 99acres and MagicBricks. Most real estate businesses need one or two of these.

faqs.question: What do large Indian developer websites include?
faqs.answer: Large developers' homepages typically let buyers browse or search projects by city, offer enquiry, callback or site-visit options, sometimes with WhatsApp, and have an NRI section with FAQs. A small builder doesn't need all of it, only the features that answer its own buyers' questions fastest.

faqs.question: What sections should a project page have?
faqs.answer: A hero with the key facts and one button, highlights, floor plans and prices, location with travel times, amenities, dated construction status, about the developer, FAQs on payment plans, loans and possession, and a short enquiry form with a WhatsApp option. Repeat the call to action through the page.

faqs.question: Should a real estate website show prices?
faqs.answer: Showing at least a starting price or price band helps. It filters out buyers who can't afford the project and saves your sales team time on unqualified calls. You can still send the full cost sheet on WhatsApp after the buyer shares their number, and label what the price includes.

faqs.question: How fast should a real estate website load?
faqs.answer: Aim for Google's "good" Core Web Vitals on mobile: main content visible within 2.5 seconds, taps answered within 200 milliseconds and almost no layout shift. Compress images, avoid autoplay videos and sliders at the top, and test with PageSpeed Insights on a mid-range phone over mobile data.

faqs.question: Does a real estate website need the RERA number?
faqs.answer: Yes, for registered projects. Pages and ads that advertise a registered project should show its RERA registration number and the state RERA website address, and brokers should show their own agent registration number. Buyers look for it as proof that the project and the seller are legitimate.

faqs.question: How do I track leads from my real estate website?
faqs.answer: Install Google Analytics 4 and your ad platform tags, mark form submissions, WhatsApp clicks and calls as conversions, and save the UTM source with every lead in your sheet or CRM. Then you can judge campaigns on cost per site visit instead of cost per click or cost per lead.
